requirements.text: the five META tools (catalog / describe / read / write / delete) - the mechanism.
discovery is R1: the generated catalog (kimai_catalog) + kimai_describe; the Kimai registry has no cross-resource resolve operation.
one bounded helper-tier read per workflowResource: true resource; where a resource has no search helper, its bounded week/status read stands in.
writes are NOT in the core: they are reachable through kimai_write / kimai_delete, dry-run first, destructive calls confirmation-gated.

toolTextOverrides.kimai_add_activity_to_team: Add one activity to a team's activity list (the activity becomes available to the team's members). Not to be confused with kimai_grant_team_activity_access, which grants the team access rights to the activity. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_activity: Create a new activity. Use for a genuinely new activity; for any change to an existing one use kimai_update_activity. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_activity_rate: Add one billing rate to an activity (rates drive timesheet billing). Distinct from kimai_delete_activity_rate (removal) and kimai_get_activity_rates (read). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_activity_rate: Delete a billing rate from an activity. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_create_activity_rate.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_activity_rates: Get the billing rates of one activity (by activity id). Read-only; returns the full rate records. For the activity plus its rates, comments and meta in one call use the kimai_read dispatch on activities.get (or the customer/project context helpers when available).
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_activities: Search activities with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (a non-integer or out-of-range value throws KimaiConfigError — never silently clamped). Compact ActivitySummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records. Activity ids from these rows feed the activity filter of kimai_search_timesheets and kimai_create_timesheet.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_activity: Update an existing activity: replaces its editable fields (name, customer reference, colour, active state). For a new activity use kimai_create_activity. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_activity_meta: Replace the custom meta fields of one activity (the meta map is replaced wholesale, not merged). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_submit_for_approval: Submit one calendar week of timesheets for approval and return the approval URL. Pass the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) identifying the week; omit `user` for the API-key owner. Dry-run first: dry_run: true validates and returns the plan without submitting.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_next_approval_week: Get the next week that still requires approval for a user, so an agent can pick the week to submit. Omit `user` for the API-key owner.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_overtime_year: Get the yearly overtime summary for a user (total and per-week breakdown) for the year of the given ISO date. Omit `user` for the API-key owner.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_week_status: Get the approval status of one calendar week for a user: whether it is approved plus its timesheets and total duration. Pass the ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) that identifies the week; omit `user` for the API-key owner.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_weekly_overtime: Get the weekly overtime entries for a user around the given ISO date. Omit `user` for the API-key owner.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_colors: Get the instance's configured colour codes (UI configuration). Call only if the user explicitly asks for instance configuration; not part of the time-tracking workflows.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_timesheet_config: Get the instance's timesheet configuration (UI defaults such as the default activity). Call only if the user explicitly asks for instance configuration; not part of the time-tracking workflows.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_add_customer_to_team: Add one customer to a team's customer list (the customer becomes available to the team's members). Not to be confused with kimai_grant_team_customer_access, which grants the team access rights to the customer. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_customer: Create a new customer. Use for a genuinely new customer; for any change to an existing one use kimai_update_customer. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_customer_comment: Add a comment to a customer (free-text note visible in the Kimai UI; pin with kimai_pin_customer_comment). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_customer_rate: Add one billing rate to a customer. Distinct from kimai_delete_customer_rate (removal) and kimai_get_customer_rates (read). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_customer_comment: Delete a comment from a customer. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_customer_rate: Delete a billing rate from a customer. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_create_customer_rate.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_customer_rates: Get the billing rates of one customer (by customer id). Read-only; returns the full rate records. For the customer with rates + comments + meta in one call use kimai_get_customer_context.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_list_customer_comments: List the comments on one customer (by customer id). Read-only. For a customer with comments + rates + meta in one call use kimai_get_customer_context.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_pin_customer_comment: Pin (or unpin) a customer comment so it stays visible in the Kimai UI comment list. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_customers: Search customers with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100. Compact CustomerSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records. Use kimai_resolve_customer to turn a name into one id.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_customer: Update an existing customer: replaces its editable fields (name, number, currency, colour, active state). For a new customer use kimai_create_customer. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_customer_meta: Replace the custom meta fields of one customer (the meta map is replaced wholesale, not merged). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_export_template: Delete an export template from the Kimai instance. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key; removing a template breaks anything that exports by its name.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_invoices: Search invoices with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (out-of-range throws KimaiConfigError). The endpoint is paginated: search reads at most ceil(limit/size) pages and returns compact InvoiceSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records. Invoice ids from these rows feed kimai_resolve_invoice.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_invoice_custom_fields: Update the custom fields of one invoice (free-form key/value map, replaced wholesale). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_add_project_to_team: Add one project to a team's project list (the project becomes available to the team's members). Not to be confused with kimai_grant_team_project_access, which grants the team access rights to the project. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_project: Create a new project (optionally for an existing customer). Use for a genuinely new project; for any change to an existing one use kimai_update_project. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_project_comment: Add a comment to a project (free-text note visible in the Kimai UI; pin with kimai_pin_project_comment). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_project_rate: Add one billing rate to a project. Distinct from kimai_delete_project_rate (removal) and kimai_get_project_rates (read). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_project_comment: Delete a comment from a project. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_delete_project_rate: Delete a billing rate from a project. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_create_project_rate.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_project_rates: Get the billing rates of one project (by project id). Read-only; returns the full rate records. For the project with customer + rates + meta in one call use kimai_get_project_context.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_list_project_comments: List the comments on one project (by project id). Read-only. For a project with comments + rates + meta in one call use kimai_get_project_context.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_pin_project_comment: Pin (or unpin) a project comment so it stays visible in the Kimai UI comment list. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_projects: Search projects with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100. Filter by customer/activity ids from kimai_search_customers / kimai_search_activities. Compact ProjectSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_project: Update an existing project: replaces its editable fields (name, customer, team, colour, active state). For a new project use kimai_create_project. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_project_meta: Replace the custom meta fields of one project (the meta map is replaced wholesale, not merged). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_list_plugins: List the plugins installed on the Kimai server, with name and version. Call it to discover optional vendor features before assuming one is absent.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_version: Get the Kimai server version (version string, version id, copyright). Useful before relying on an endpoint that a specific server version introduced.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_ping: Health-check the Kimai instance. Returns true when the API is reachable. Call it first to verify connectivity and credentials.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_tag: Create a new tag. The vendor exposes no tag update, so renaming a tag is a create + delete pair (kimai_create_tag then kimai_delete_tag). Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_tags: Search tags with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (out-of-range throws KimaiConfigError). Compact TagSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records. Tag names/ids from these rows feed the tags filter of kimai_search_timesheets.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_add_team_member: Add a user as a member of a team (membership only — it does not grant the member access to specific customers/projects/activities). Use kimai_remove_team_member to take a member off. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_team: Create a new team. Use for a genuinely new team; for any change to an existing one use kimai_update_team. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_grant_team_activity_access: Grant a team access rights to one activity (the team's members may log against it). Inverse: kimai_revoke_team_activity_access. Do not confuse with kimai_add_activity_to_team, which only lists the activity under the team. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_grant_team_customer_access: Grant a team access rights to one customer. Inverse: kimai_revoke_team_customer_access. Do not confuse with kimai_add_customer_to_team, which only lists the customer under the team. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_grant_team_project_access: Grant a team access rights to one project. Inverse: kimai_revoke_team_project_access. Do not confuse with kimai_add_project_to_team, which only lists the project under the team. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_list_teams: List all teams. The vendor returns the complete unpaginated batch in one call — teams have no paging and no text search, so this is the read tool for the resource. Output is the full Team records, including members and the customers/projects/activities access lists. Use kimai_resolve_team to turn a name into one id.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_remove_team_member: Remove a user from a team (team membership only; the user's individual access grants to customers/projects/activities are untouched). Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_add_team_member.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_revoke_team_activity_access: Revoke a team's access rights to one activity (its members can no longer log against it). Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_grant_team_activity_access.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_revoke_team_customer_access: Revoke a team's access rights to one customer. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_grant_team_customer_access.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_revoke_team_project_access: Revoke a team's access rights to one project. Destructive and confirm-gated: confirm must equal the operation key. Inverse of kimai_grant_team_project_access.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_team: Update an existing team: replaces its editable fields (name, description, membership is managed via add/remove member, not here). For a new team use kimai_create_team. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_timesheet: Create a timesheet. Requires project + activity (vendor); begin is vendor-required — the dry run warns when it is missing. Find the ids with kimai_search_projects / kimai_search_activities and the user id with kimai_search_users or kimai_get_current_user. Dry-run first: dry_run: true validates and returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_recent_timesheets: Get the most recent timesheets from the dedicated vendor endpoint: a fixed small unfiltered batch, no paging parameters, caller-scoped to what the API key can see. Use for a quick "what was logged lately" glance; for any filter, a date range or a larger set use kimai_search_timesheets.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_timesheets: Search timesheets with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (out of range throws KimaiConfigError — never silently clamped). Without a user filter the SDK passes user=all (requires the vendor view_other_timesheet permission). Find activity/project/customer ids with kimai_search_activities / kimai_search_projects / kimai_search_customers. Compact TimesheetSummary rows by default; expand: true for the full records.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_create_user: Create a new user (admin only). Use for a genuinely new user; for any change to an existing one use kimai_update_user. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_get_current_user: Get the user record of the API key this request was made with (the "current user": id, name, department, preferences). Use when you need "my" user id — e.g. as the user filter of a search, or the owner default for week tools — without searching users. Read-only; returns the full typed record.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_search_users: Search users with the spec filters, bounded by an explicit limit. limit defaults to 25, hard max 100 (out-of-range throws KimaiConfigError). Compact UserSummary rows by default (no credential fields); expand: true for the full records. User ids from these rows feed the user filter of kimai_search_timesheets / kimai_get_week_status and the users list of kimai_team_week.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_user: Update an existing user (admin, or self for own editable fields): replaces the editable fields. For a new user use kimai_create_user. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.
toolTextOverrides.kimai_update_user_preferences: Update the UI preferences (language, timezone, theme, rows per page) of one user. Admin or self only. Dry-run first: dry_run: true returns the plan without writing.

servedTextRule: Served description of a dedicated tool: a curated description override (MCP_TOOL_OVERRIDES.json, mirrored in TOOL_TEXT_OVERRIDES) is the SINGLE source - serve it verbatim; the generator appends no mechanical bounds sentence on top of a curated text. A tool without an override serves the registry metadata.purpose, then metadata.usage when present and different, then the mechanical bounds sentence derived from effect, flags, pagination, resolution and compact. Catalog rows: summary = a curated summary override else the registry purpose; when = a curated when override else the registry preferredWhen. Closed input contracts: a curated paramDescription override else the registry field description.

metaTools.name: kimai_catalog
metaTools.title: Discover Operations (Catalog)
metaTools.description: List the capabilities the node-kimai registry implements with the tool that exposes each one (when it has one), its effect, whether it needs a dry run or a confirmation flag, and the arguments it requires. The tool list on this server is a SUBSET: this is a curated core profile, and the catalog is how you discover a capability that has no tool of its own — find the row, call kimai_describe for the exact schema, then kimai_read/kimai_write/kimai_delete. Bounded: limit defaults to 40 and is hard-capped at 100; prefer a filter over dumping the catalog.

metaTools.name: kimai_describe
metaTools.title: Describe One Operation
metaTools.description: Return the full input schema, effect, flags, dry-run support, error vocabulary, related operations and preferredWhen guidance for ONE registry operation, so a capability can be called correctly without carrying every schema in context. Use it after kimai_catalog named the operation and before kimai_read/kimai_write/kimai_delete. Takes the canonical operation key exactly as the catalog prints it (for example "timesheets.search") — never a tool name, and there is no fuzzy matching: an unknown key is a CONFIG_ERROR naming the nearest catalog keys.

metaTools.name: kimai_read
metaTools.title: Read One Registry Operation
metaTools.description: Execute only effect "read" operations by canonical registry key. Prefer the dedicated bounded search/resolve tools where they exist; use this dispatch for a read with no dedicated tool. `input` is a CLOSED per-operation contract: exactly the operation's declared fields — an unknown field is refused with a typed CONFIG_ERROR before any request. Reads have no dry run and never mutate.

metaTools.name: kimai_write
metaTools.title: Write One Registry Operation
metaTools.description: Execute only effect "write" operations by canonical registry key. Mutations default to a dry-run preview (dry_run: true returns the plan; the request is never issued); dry_run: false executes. `input` is a CLOSED per-operation contract — an unknown field is refused before any request. A destructive operation is REFUSED here; use kimai_delete.

metaTools.name: kimai_delete
metaTools.title: Delete One Registry Operation
metaTools.description: Execute only effect "destructive" operations by canonical registry key. Destructive calls are irreversible and REFUSED without `confirm` equal to the operation key. `input` is a CLOSED per-operation contract. Neither the preview nor the confirmation string is human consent: the host must enforce its own approval policy.
